brief: Goldman Sachs raises its global data center capacity forecast to 217GW by 2030 (from 168GW in February 2026), implying 116GW of net additions and roughly $6tn of capex at a $50bn/GW rule of thumb, which GS says is covered by ~$1tn/year of consensus hyperscale capex. GS has turned more positive on neoclouds after recent lease and GPU-as-a-service deals, and flags Nvidia's new credit-support and revenue-share model with Sharon AI and Firmus as lowering neocloud cost of capital for smaller, shorter-term buildouts. Off this capacity growth plus updated server-shipment and regional power forecasts, GS raises 2030 global data center power demand growth to 170% versus 2025 (from 117% previously), framing the buildout around seven constraints: AI pervasiveness, chip/server efficiency, power pricing, policy, parts availability, people availability, and physical siting risk. US demand should reach ~108GW by 2030, led by PJM, then MISO overtaking ERCOT. GS stays Buy on regulated utilities and IPPs (FE, XEL, DUK, SRE, TLN, VST, NRG) as beneficiaries, Buy on DLR, and Neutral on EQIX and IREN.
